---
title: "Course alignment and documentation governance"
---

## Faculty final-delivery alignment

The final-delivery guidance requires **three coordinated deliverables**, all describing the same release and scope.

| Deliverable | What it contains | Status (November 27) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Complete product handoff | The tagged release of the repository: code, processed data (data-v0.7), 320 automated tests and 198 data checks, scores (scoring v0.5), dashboard v1.0, the runbook (`docs/runbook.md`) and this book | Code freeze November 27, 6 PM; the release tag follows. BankUnited downloads the final tagged release; InfoSec review in progress |
| 2. Working final demonstration | A live dashboard walkthrough on the same release, with one traceable finding (Charlotte, #18 of 190) and one missing-data exception (Hartford) | December 4, at BankUnited |
| 3. Short executive deck | Five core slides: business problem and users, delivered solution and user journey, logic and methodology, results and validation, handoff and next steps | December 4, at BankUnited |

## Where the other guidance items are covered

| Guidance item | Where it is covered |
|---|---|
| Decision story | Scope chapter: the tool ranks metro markets for further investigation; the entry decision stays with BankUnited |
| Semantic contract | Data dictionary chapter (each table's grain and key, and each column's meaning and type) and data decisions D1–D15 |
| Model evaluation and point-in-time use | Weights are set by the team and BankUnited, not fitted to outcomes, so there are no training splits. Point-in-time runs use `python -m src.scoring.run --as-of <date>` with the release dates in `data/reference/release_dates.csv` |
| Architecture and interfaces | Technical handoff chapter and the runbook: setup, keys, refresh steps and troubleshooting |
| Methodology and worked example | Methodology chapter: pillars, measures, weights and the multifamily test; the dashboard chapter's key insights walk through Charlotte's result |
| Reproducibility | Validation chapter: clean-clone reruns, the dashboard v1.0 user test and the pre-freeze regression |
| Sign-offs and sponsor access | Acceptance chapter |

**Important scope statement:** `dashboard/README.md` (v1.0) describes a Market Attractiveness score with filters for population, distance and industry fit; a combined Fit score is not built. The demo and final report must not claim a complete two-score product unless implementation evidence is subsequently supplied.

**Guidance source:** `Practicum Guidance Final Delivery Package.pdf`, pp. 1–3 and 6–9.
